The shares themselves are measured-physical upstream: CAMPD observed heat-rate curves and measured duct-fire headroom, per the generic table's own provenance comments.

disclosures.note: SOCO-40 determination basis — the six lines PRECOMMIT §10 requires, plus this lane's own 2025 hydro input hole. Reported, never patched (rules 1 / 13 / 14). Nothing here is corrected, excluded or tuned around.
disclosures.1_the_price_gap: NO PUBLIC SOCO PRICE EXISTS AND NONE EVER WILL. SOCO's footprint publishes no LMP, hub or clearing price, so data/raw/_validation-source/actual_lmp.json carries no SOCO block and MUST NOT GAIN ONE — a placeholder would break calibration_verdict._price_reference_absent and silently move SOCO onto the ordinary determination path. C3a (price level), C3b (price shape) and C3c (price tail / scarcity) are therefore UNSCORABLE — NOT FAILED. The determination ceiling is rubric v3.8 PHYSICALLY-CALIBRATED (PRICE UNSCORED); this run can never read CALIBRATED. Gate G17 stands: no neighbouring hub, no proxy, no cost-stack reconstruction, ever. The model's own load-weighted mean price is printed as MODEL-ONLY / UNVERIFIED and is not evidence of price skill. SOCO-13's NO is the governing ruling.
disclosures.2_R_i_pumped_storage_unobservable: 1,306.6 MW of pumped storage is UNOBSERVABLE in EIA-930: 0 of 8,760 hours in 2023 and 99.7 % of 2024. NG: WAT is never negative before the 2024-07-15 cut-over, so PS charging was NOT REPORTED rather than folded into hydro. This is a hard constraint on the C1 fuelmix benchmark itself, never a hole to fill: the model dispatches 1.80 / 1.46 / 2.39 TWh of PS discharge against an EIA-930 comparator that exists only for 2025 (1.96 TWh).
disclosures.3_card_S3_southern_power_excluded: The zonal shares are built from FIVE fully-cited FERC-714 respondents (Alabama Power, Georgia Power, Mississippi Power, Oglethorpe 107, MEAG 210). Southern Power (respondent 186) is EXCLUDED — a documented NO: nothing establishes where its FERC-714 planning-area load sits. Its 3.211 / 3.401 / 3.084 TWh is named here and never absorbed. The owner chose the cited five over the six-respondent set whose residual is smaller (1.63 / 1.50 / -0.03 %) precisely because the smaller residual rested on an uncited component (rule 13).

disclosures.6_R_w_oil_false_positive_DISCHARGED: DISCHARGED BY THIS RUN, AND MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. PRECOMMIT §10 line 6 recorded the SOCO 2024 NG: OIL rule-14 false positive: the EIA-930 unit-slip screen deleted 4.4 GWh of a REAL Winter Storm Heather oil run (2024-01-17 03:00-09:00, 530 -> 649 -> 660 -> 687 -> 762 -> 801 -> 350 MW, tracking SOCO demand from 41.0 to 47.4 GW), biasing the C1 oil benchmark LOW. Between arm A's basis (13198951) and this keeper's pin (71884144), lane NWPP-39 landed a zero-baseline guard on that screen (_FUEL_SPIKE_PLATEAU_PCT = 99.0): a series whose p99.9 is itself more than _FUEL_SPIKE_RATIO times its p99.0 has a tail rather than a plateau at the top, the screen's own premise is falsified by the series, and the column passes through untouched. MEASURED ON THE TWO LAUNCH LOGS: arm A repairs SOCO NG: OIL 2023 h7975 and 2024 h386-392; THIS RUN REPAIRS NEITHER, while the GENUINE 2025 NG: NG spikes (70,683 MW in a 32,574 MW hour, four hours) still fire in BOTH. Releasing the false positives while keeping the true ones is the discriminating signature. The 2024 EIA-930 oil benchmark moves 0.00 -> 0.01 TWh accordingly. This was audited and declared as the single LIVE G-DRIFT hunk BEFORE the solve (docs/handoffs/ADDENDUM-soco40-armB-relaunch-and-gdrift-2026-09-16.md §3.1), not discovered in the result.
disclosures.7_2025_hydro_input_hole: NOT A MODEL DEFECT — AN INPUT HOLE, NAMED IN PRECOMMIT §4.5 BEFORE THE SOLVE. The EIA-923 hydro budget for 2025 resolves only 5 plants / 0.3275 TWh / 368 MW against 6.01 TWh measured by EIA-930, where 2023 and 2024 resolve 42 plants / 6.82 and 6.30 TWh. The LP is handed ~5.7 TWh less hydro than the year actually had. Consequences, reported at full magnitude and NOT absorbed: (a) coal backfills it — COAL_PRB 31.541 and COAL_BIT 16.121 TWh in 2025 against 2024's 22.420 / 12.256, so 2025 coal runs 47.66 TWh against 44.08 measured; (b) the LP cannot serve 13 summer afternoon hours and posts 8,930 MWh of slack at VOLL 61,900 $/MWh (2025-06-25 15-17h, 07-29 12-16h, 08-18 13-15h, 09-05 13-14h), which is what drags the 2025 MODEL-ONLY mean price to 136.40 $/MWh against 32.49 / 30.22 in 2023 / 2024. NO REPAIR WAS ARMED: --hydro-backfill-year and --hydro-eia930-monthly were deliberately NOT passed (PRECOMMIT §3.1), because arming a one-year input repair inside the first keeper is a lever decision the desk queue owns, not this lane's. Routed as SOCO's next data-intake item.
disclosures.8_what_the_coal_split_did_and_did_not_do: The owner's instruction is executed and the single coal class is GONE: every year now carries COAL_BIT and COAL_PRB and no bare COAL (machine-verified on all three class_hourly parquets). It is a RECLASSIFICATION, not a re-dispatch: every non-coal class is byte-identical to arm A, COAL_BIT + COAL_PRB sums to arm A's bare COAL to the GWh in all three years (33.142 / 34.676 / 47.662), and the 2023 and 2024 P0 objectives are IDENTICAL to arm A's to the cent (3690944814.1196 and 3398767416.6013). Only 2025's objective moves (5682126660.3872 -> 5680277825.0155), in the scarcity hours the hydro hole creates. What it BUYS is that C1's coal rows now score against the benchmark's own EIA-923 fuel-code rows instead of one blended class against two — the SPP-40 §7.3 defect — and that D-1 now resolves its shape miss to COAL_BIT specifically rather than to a blended COAL.
